That conclusion is emitted by GitHub's runner, which a contributor can trigger but cannot author, so moving the test's exit code into that job replaces an author-set field with a producer outside the write boundary. Half two is the operands: the gaps doctor.sh --strict counts are reads of governance markdown and state stamps the actor writes, which is paperwork against paperwork regardless of where the script came from. The four anchored producers available are grep over committed bytes, a python literal/token scan, a token-vs-mark comparison, and GitHub's Pages deployment service; none of them emits a signal about whether this workspace complies with the primitive contract.

Vendoring bstack into the repo with a checksum is a supply-chain policy choice, and even once taken it fixes only the provenance half — the check would still be comparing documents the author wrote in the same commit, so it would not measure as anchored. Grounding the claim needs an outside referent for the primitive contract (a published spec, an executed behaviour per primitive, or a third-party consumer), which is a change to what the check asserts. Note also that the CI surface that would matter here was not measured: the fixture sampled 15 of 69 nodes and .github/workflows/portability.yml's own steps are absent, so a route onto the runner cannot be proposed from this graph even if one exists. That is a gap in coverage, and it is reported rather than guessed.
